business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K Item 1 business description.
business_model.claim: Wabash makes money by designing, manufacturing and servicing transport equipment: dry and refrigerated van trailers, platform and tank trailers, truck bodies, composite panels and food-grade processing equipment. It also sells parts, services and leased trailers.
quotes: we design, manufacture, and service a diverse range of products supporting first-to-final mile operations

business_model.basis: Segment structure and dealer network are stated in the 10-K Item 1. The split between direct and dealer sales is not given.
business_model.claim: Results are reported in two segments: Transportation Solutions (trailers, truck bodies, tank trailers) and Parts & Services (aftermarket parts, upfitting, process systems, composites, TaaS). Products reach customers through dealers and preferred partners as well as directly.
quotes: manages its business in two operating and reportable segments
our extensive dealer and preferred partner network

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K risk factors; the customer type is inferred from the risk factor text and the product list.
business_model.claim: Customers are mainly trucking, logistics and transportation fleets, with some concentration: the five largest accounted for about 35% of 2025 net sales, no single customer exceeded 10%, and international sales were under 10%.
quotes: our five largest customers together accounted for approximately 35% of our aggregate net sales in 2025

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K Item 1 and MD&A.
business_model.claim: Revenue in Transportation Solutions follows trailer demand, which depends on freight volumes and is cyclical. In 2025 total net sales fell 20.8%: Transportation Solutions fell 23.4% while Parts & Services rose 15.6%.
quotes: Trailer demand is a direct function of the amount of freight to be transported.
The decrease in shipments was primarily driven by lower demand due to the softening freight market.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-Q MD&A and income statement.
business_model.claim: In Q3 2026 net sales rose 24.8% to 476,408 (table in thousands) from 381,595, driven by new trailer shipments (9,563 versus 6,675 units). Truck body shipments fell (1,685 versus 3,067).
quotes: The growth in revenue from new trailer shipments outpaced the reduction in revenue from lower truck body shipments.

business_model.claim: The main cost is cost of sales, which is mostly materials (variable) plus manufacturing costs such as labor and overhead (fixed and variable). Q3 2026 gross profit was 14,875 (table in thousands) on sales of 476,408, a 3.1% margin. Segment gross margins were 1.0% for Transportation Solutions and 15.7% for Parts & Services.
quotes: Cost of sales is comprised of material costs, a variable expense, and other manufacturing costs, comprised of both fixed and variable expenses, including direct and indirect labor, outbound freight, overhead expenses, and depreciation.

business_model.claim: Q3 2026 cost of sales rose by more than revenue in Transportation Solutions, mainly from materials and labor. This included production-readiness costs to prepare dry van lines for higher 2027 output, so margin fell despite higher sales.
quotes: The increase in cost of sales was primarily attributable to increases of approximately $76.7 million in material costs and $4.9 million in labor costs, as well as other production-readiness costs.

business_model.basis: The strategy is stated in the 10-K. The Q3 detail is stated in the 10-Q. That the segment will be less cyclical is management's expectation, not a result.
business_model.claim: Parts & Services is the smaller, higher-margin and growing segment that management expects to be less cyclical. In Q3 2026 its sales growth came from upfit and services, partly offset by weaker aftermarket parts, and its margin fell on start-up and expansion costs.
quotes: we expect to achieve a larger base of less cyclical sales and profit
higher sales within our upfit and services businesses of approximately $9.1 million

business_model.basis: Stated in the earnings release and the 10-K risk factors.

quotes: ACT is forecasting annual new trailer production levels for 2027, 2028, 2029, and 2030 of approximately 257,000, 297,000, 307,000, and 299,000, respectively.

growth_thesis.basis: The sales growth is stated in the 10-Q; the strategy is stated in the 10-K.

For the segment to add to profit growth, these costs have to be absorbed by volume.
